summary: Closes two narrow runtime-quality defects: durably cancelled SubAgent children no longer remain visible as active sessions, and proc-version unit fixtures no longer inherit the production dual-root source anchor. Exact execution authority and production workspace semantics remain unchanged.

evidence: Production-shaped RED reproduced a child whose terminal receipt said child_outcome=cancelled while Session.status remained active.
The implementation requires a durable result, successful same-generation topology terminal write, and exact outcome=cancelled before SessionStore.archive.
Normal completed children are regression-tested to remain active/session-visible and AgentFollowup behavior remains unchanged.
components.verification_level: TDD RED/GREEN plus 106-test SubAgent adjacency, whole-tree static/security gates, and full committed-state repository CI

If the archive projection fails, generation cleanup continues and the child remains visible rather than being falsely hidden.
components.rollback_route: Revert the SubAgent fix commit; no persistent schema migration or LFRT/8901 change is involved, and existing durable topology history remains valid.

g1.necessity: A child that has durably terminated as cancelled must not continue to appear in the active-session index, but execution outcome authority must remain in the durable SubAgent topology rather than being duplicated into a new Session status schema.

g2.authority_owner: existing SubAgent topology/EventStore for exact execution outcome plus existing SessionStore active/archive lifecycle for visibility
g2.non_duplication: The change does not create a new execution-state owner. It projects only a durably confirmed cancelled terminal into the existing archive lifecycle; completed children retain the existing active visibility used by AgentFollowup.
